Search documentation Ctrl K Ask AI Log in Set up Copy page Copied You need an install token for all projects. Then you add one more item, which depends on where the package runs: Where the package runs What you add All projects An install token in .npmrc A server (Node, a worker, a script) REDUCTO_API_KEY in its environment A browser editor The license proxy on your backend, and proxyUrl when you mount the editor A sandboxed server (no internet or no API key) The license proxy on your backend, and REDUCTO_LICENSE_PROXY in the serverâs environment 1. Install with an install token An install token ( rnpm_â¦ ) lets npm install download the @reductoai/* packages from npm.reducto.ai . Make one on the Office SDK page in Reducto Studio. Studio gives you two lines for .npmrc : @reductoai : registry=https://npm.reducto.ai/ //npm.reducto.ai/ : _authToken=rnpm_... Then install as usual: npm install @ reductoai/docx If npm install fails with 403 , your lockfile or package.json asks for a version that your token cannot install. To fix it, run npm install @reductoai/docx . About tokens: Make one token for each machine or CI job. Give it a label that tells which one. There is no limit on the number of tokens. You see the token one time only. If you lose it, make a new one. All tokens of your organization install the same package. Lockfile hashes are the same on all machines. When you revoke a token, new installs with it fail. Copies that you installed before continue to work. Self-serve tokens install @reductoai/docx , @reductoai/docx-editor , @reductoai/viewer and @reductoai/portable-fonts . The PowerPoint and Excel packages are in private preview with alpha customers. Contact us to get access. 2. On a server: set REDUCTO_API_KEY In Node, the package reads REDUCTO_API_KEY from the environment. You do not change your code: REDUCTO_API_KEY =< your API key > node edit.mjs Use a key from the same Reducto organization that made the install token. A server that runs a copy not installed through your install token, such as a prebuilt image, reads its license from REDUCTO_LICENSE . Copy the JSON from node_modules/@reductoai/docx/reducto-license.js of an install from npm.reducto.ai : REDUCTO_LICENSE = '{"id":"lic_â¦","endpoint":"https://npm.reducto.ai/-/license"}' REDUCTO_API_KEY =< your API key > node edit.mjs The license in the package wins over REDUCTO_LICENSE . Either way, nothing opens until npm.reducto.ai trusts it. 3. In a browser: add the license proxy Do not put your Reducto API key in a page, because all users can read it. A browser editor sends its license traffic to your backend, and your backend adds the key. Without a proxy, a browser editor does not run. On your backend , add licenseProxy() behind your own login check. It forwards only license checks and usage reports to npm.reducto.ai (or office-license.reducto.ai ) and adds your API key. It answers 404 to all other requests. A Next.js route: // app/reducto/[...path]/route.ts import { licenseProxy } from "@reductoai/docx/license-proxy" ; import { getSession } from "@/lib/auth" ; // your app's login check const proxy = licenseProxy () ; export async function POST ( request : Request ) { if ( ! ( await getSession ( request ))) { return new Response ( "unauthorized" , { status : 401 }) ; } return proxy ( request ) ; } licenseProxy() returns a (request: Request) => Promise<Response> function. It works without changes in Next.js route handlers, Hono, Cloudflare Workers, Deno and Bun. Options: Option Default apiKey process.env.REDUCTO_API_KEY upstream process.env.REDUCTO_LICENSE_ENDPOINT , else https://npm.reducto.ai fetch The global fetch Express does not give you a Request , so wrap the proxy: import express from "express" ; import { licenseProxy } from "@reductoai/docx/license-proxy" ; const proxy = licenseProxy () ; const app = express () ; app . post ( [ "/reducto/-/license" , "/reducto/-/events" ] , requireLogin , // your app's login middleware express . text ({ type : "*/*" }) , async ( req , res ) => { const answer = await proxy ( new Request ( `http://localhost ${ req . path } ` , { method : "POST" , headers : { "content-type" : req . get ( "content-type" ) ?? "text/plain" } , body : req . body , }) , ) ; res . status ( answer . status ) . type ( answer . headers . get ( "content-type" ) ?? "application/json" ) . send ( await answer . text ()) ; } , ) ; In the page , give the routeâs base path as proxyUrl : import { mountDocxEditor } from "@reductoai/docx-editor" ; mountDocxEditor ( "#editor" , { proxyUrl : "/reducto" }) ; The same backend route serves @reductoai/pptx-editor ( mountPptxEditor("#editor", { proxyUrl: "/reducto" }) ) and @reductoai/xlsx-editor ( mountXlsxEditor("#editor", { proxyUrl: "/reducto" }) ). Each SDK also exports licenseProxy from @reductoai/{docx,pptx,xlsx}/license-proxy . If you use a headless editor model instead of mount*Editor , call useProxy("/reducto") from the editor package once at startup. Warning The proxy is required. A browser editor without one sends no license traffic and opens no document: it shows âYour package isnât configured properly.â 4. In a sandbox: point the server at the license proxy A server that cannot reach npm.reducto.ai , or that must not hold your API key, sends its license traffic through the license proxy instead. Mount licenseProxy() on a backend that can reach npm.reducto.ai (step 3), then set REDUCTO_LICENSE_PROXY in the sandbox: REDUCTO_LICENSE_PROXY = https : //your-backend.example/reducto node edit.mjs The sandbox needs no REDUCTO_API_KEY : the proxy adds it. To set the address in code instead, call useProxy(url) from @reductoai/docx/license-proxy once at startup (it takes precedence over REDUCTO_LICENSE_PROXY ). Firewalls and networks with no internet access The package connects only to Reducto, over HTTPS on port 443. If your network blocks outbound traffic, allow these connections: Machine Why it connects Host CI and build machines npm install npm.reducto.ai Servers that run the package, or the backend with the license proxy License checks and usage reports, at least one time in 65 minutes npm.reducto.ai , or office-license.reducto.ai for a fixed IP address Browsers and sandboxed servers using the proxy They do not connect. They send traffic only to your backend None If your firewall accepts hostnames Allow npm.reducto.ai . You do not need to change anything else. If your firewall accepts only IP addresses npm.reducto.ai is served through Cloudflare, and its IP addresses can change without notice. For license checks and usage reports, use office-license.reducto.ai instead. It has one fixed IP address that does not change. Look up the address one time, and allow it on port 443: dig + short office-license.reducto.ai On each server that runs the package, and on the backend with the license proxy, set: REDUCTO_LICENSE_ENDPOINT = https : //office-license.reducto.ai The package then sends its license checks and usage reports there. licenseProxy() forwards there too, unless you give it upstream . Browsers need nothing, because they connect only to your backend. office-license.reducto.ai serves license checks and usage reports only, not npm install . Your CI and build machines still install from npm.reducto.ai . If they can allow only IP addresses, allow Cloudflareâs published ranges , or contact support@reducto.ai . Warning There is no offline license. If a system cannot connect to Reducto for more than 65 minutes, the package stops with ReductoLicenseError ( unverified ). For an air-gapped network, contact support@reducto.ai before you deploy. Make sure that the setup works Open a document. The package checks its license on first use. If the document does not open and you see âYour package isnât configured properly.â, see Troubleshooting . Look at the console. If there are no warnings from Reducto, the setup is correct.
